name: murphy-network-extra
description: Extra vetted network-stack sysctls (CIS Linux 3.x). Absent keys SKIP, never false-fail.

rules.title: Not sending ICMP redirects
rules.rationale: A host that sends ICMP redirects can be used to reshape a neighbour's routing — only routers should.

rules.title: Default iface not sending ICMP redirects
rules.rationale: Same as above, applied to interfaces brought up later.

rules.title: Default iface ignores ICMP redirects
rules.rationale: Accepting redirects lets an on-path attacker reroute your traffic through them.

rules.title: Default iface drops source-routed packets
rules.rationale: Source routing lets a packet dictate its own return path — a spoofing aid.

rules.title: Impossible (martian) packets are logged
rules.rationale: Logging spoofed/impossible source addresses gives you an early warning of address spoofing.

rules.title: Ignoring ICMP echo to broadcast
rules.rationale: Answering broadcast pings makes the host a Smurf-amplification reflector.

rules.title: Ignoring bogus ICMP error responses
rules.rationale: Drops malformed ICMP errors that would otherwise spam the logs and can aid teardown attacks.

rules.title: Reverse-path filter on default iface
rules.rationale: Reverse-path filtering drops packets whose source couldn't legitimately arrive on that interface. Strict RPF (1) can break VPNs / asymmetric routing, so autopilot only touches it at --risk medium.

rules.title: IPv6 router advertisements not blindly accepted
rules.rationale: Blindly accepting IPv6 RAs lets a rogue router on the LAN become your default gateway — but disabling RA breaks IPv6 autoconfig on most desktops, so this is advisory only, not auto-fixed.
rules.fix: On hosts that aren't IPv6 routers, set net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_ra=0.

rules.title: IPv6 ICMP redirects ignored
rules.rationale: The IPv6 twin of the redirect-reroute attack.
